214	Clicking a subfolder header selects all files in that group. Clicking a file selects it and loads its pages into the thumbnail strip and detail panel.
215	
216	### Drive folder assignment
217	
218	- Clicking a Drive folder field (on a subfolder header or an individual file) opens a **folder browser modal** displaying the user's Drive folder tree, fetched lazily on first open. A **recently used folders** list appears at the top for quick access.
219	- Selecting multiple items (files and/or subfolders) and assigning a Drive folder applies it to all selected items at once.
220	- A subfolder's Drive folder assignment propagates to all files within it. A file-level assignment overrides the parent subfolder's.
221	
222	### Inclusion selection
223	
224	- Every subfolder and file has a checkbox controlling whether it's included in the upload. Everything starts selected on a fresh scan; this always resets to fully selected (it is not remembered across scans, unlike Drive folder mappings).
225	- Checking or unchecking a subfolder recursively sets all of its descendants (nested subfolders and files) to the same state.
226	- Unchecking a single file or subfolder underneath an otherwise fully-selected subfolder puts that subfolder into an indeterminate state; this propagates upward through ancestors as needed. Unchecking the last remaining selected descendant of a subfolder leaves it fully unselected rather than indeterminate — and that resolution is itself recursive: if that was also the last selected descendant of its own parent, the parent becomes fully unselected too, and so on up to the root. The same recursive collapse applies symmetrically in the other direction: checking the last remaining unselected descendant leaves a subfolder fully selected rather than indeterminate, propagating upward the same way.
227	- Clicking an indeterminate subfolder's checkbox selects all of its descendants (an indeterminate checkbox click always selects, never clears).
228	- A toolbar-level "Select All" / "Select None" shortcut applies to the whole tree.
229	- Excluded files and subfolders don't need a Drive destination assignment and are skipped by the pre-upload conflict check and the upload itself. They remain visible, and PDFs can still be selected for preview.
230	- Selection checkboxes are disabled once the tree is locked (same `locked` state that freezes Drive folder assignment and renaming after "Upload All" is clicked).
231	
232	### Remembered folder mappings
233	
234	The app remembers Drive folder assignments keyed on local subfolder name. When a subfolder with a previously seen name is loaded, the app auto-fills its Drive destination. The user can change it before uploading. Mappings persist across sessions.
235	
236	### Post-upload cleanup
237	
238	After a successful upload batch, the user is prompted to either delete the source files or move them to a local archive folder. The archive folder destination can be configured and is remembered across sessions.
239	
240	### Persisted settings
241	
242	- Drive folder mappings (local subfolder name → Drive folder)
243	- Recently used Drive folders
244	- Last-used root local folder
245	- Local archive folder path
246	
247	### Authentication
248	
249	Google OAuth via a browser window, triggered the first time Drive Upload mode is used. Credentials are stored locally and reused in future sessions.
250	
251	### Error handling
252	
253	If a file upload fails, the error is shown inline next to that file in the left panel. Other uploads in the batch continue unaffected. The user can retry failed uploads individually without restarting the batch.
254	
255	## Global error handling
256	
257	The mode-specific "Error handling" sections above cover *expected* error conditions the app already knows how to name and react to (unequal page counts, filename conflicts, a failed upload). This section covers the remaining case: *unexpected* errors — bugs, panics, a call site that forgot to catch a rejected promise. Today those can fail silently (a swallowed exception, a stuck spinner) with no signal that anything went wrong. The goal is a fallback net that guarantees the user is notified, without trying to name or recover from the specific failure.
258	
259	- **Frontend uncaught errors**: a top-level React error boundary around the app catches render-time exceptions, replacing the crashed subtree with a generic notice instead of a blank/frozen screen.
260	- **Frontend unhandled rejections**: a single `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` (plus `'error'` for non-promise exceptions) installed at startup shows a Mantine notification whenever an error reaches the top without having been caught by feature-specific handling. This is the backstop for the async call sites tracked in the "Various" checklist below — as those are migrated to explicit per-action error handling, this listener increasingly only fires for genuine bugs.
261	- **Backend panics**: each Wails-exposed RPC method recovers from panics and converts them into a returned error, so a bug in one RPC surfaces as a rejected JS promise (and thus hits the frontend backstop above) rather than crashing the whole process.
262	- **Presentation**: unexpected errors show a persistent (not auto-dismissing) notification — "An unexpected error occurred" plus the underlying error text. No retry/recovery is attempted automatically, since the cause is by definition unhandled and unclassified.

- Every subfolder and file has a checkbox controlling whether it's included in the upload. Everything starts selected on a fresh scan; this always resets to fully selected (it is not remembered across scans, unlike Drive folder mappings).

The same recursive collapse applies symmetrically in the other direction: checking the last remaining unselected descendant leaves a subfolder fully selected rather than indeterminate, propagating upward the same way.
- Clicking an indeterminate subfolder's checkbox selects all of its descendants (an indeterminate checkbox click always selects, never clears).

After a successful upload batch, the user is prompted to either delete the source files or move them to a local archive folder. The archive folder destination can be configured and is remembered across sessions.

- Drive folder mappings (local subfolder name → Drive folder)

- Local archive folder path

If a file upload fails, the error is shown inline next to that file in the left panel. Other uploads in the batch continue unaffected. The user can retry failed uploads individually without restarting the batch.

## Global error handling

The mode-specific "Error handling" sections above cover *expected* error conditions the app already knows how to name and react to (unequal page counts, filename conflicts, a failed upload). This section covers the remaining case: *unexpected* errors — bugs, panics, a call site that forgot to catch a rejected promise. Today those can fail silently (a swallowed exception, a stuck spinner) with no signal that anything went wrong. The goal is a fallback net that guarantees the user is notified, without trying to name or recover from the specific failure.

- **Frontend uncaught errors**: a top-level React error boundary around the app catches render-time exceptions, replacing the crashed subtree with a generic notice instead of a blank/frozen screen.

# Paper Scan Processor

A desktop application for post-processing PDF files containing batches of scanned documents. The app has three modes: **Merge**, **Split**, and **Drive Upload**.

## Tech stack

- **Desktop framework**: Wails
- **Backend**: Go
- **Frontend**: TypeScript + React
- **UI components**: Mantine
- **Virtualization**: TanStack Virtual
- **Drag-and-drop**: dnd-kit
- **PDF manipulation**: pdfcpu
- **PDF rendering** (thumbnails): `pdftoppm` (Poppler, system install, called as subprocess)

## Common elements

Both modes include a thumbnail panel and a page detail panel, and support the same per-page editing operations.

### Thumbnail panel

A vertically scrolling strip of page thumbnails. Width is user-adjustable via a drag handle; thumbnails scale to fill the panel width. Rendering is on-demand and virtualized — only visible thumbnails (plus a small overscan buffer) are rendered at any given time.

The Go backend exposes a per-page render method returning a base64-encoded PNG; the frontend requests thumbnails as they scroll into view (`pdftoppm` subprocess).

#### Keyboard shortcuts

| Key                    | Action                                     |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `R`                    | Rotate selected page clockwise 90°         |
| `Shift+R`              | Rotate selected page counter-clockwise 90° |
| `Delete` / `Backspace` | Toggle skip on the selected page           |
| `←` / `→`              | Select previous / next page                |

### Page detail panel

Shows the currently selected page at reading resolution. Selecting a thumbnail updates it.

message.content: Is it possible to expand/collapse a subfolder when there are already multiple files selected and a file within the subfolder should be added?

content.text:
Good catch — as designed, no: there's a real conflict.

- Plain click on the group header both toggles expand/collapse *and* replaces the selection with just that group — so expanding via plain click would wipe out the existing multi-selection.
- Cmd/Ctrl-click adds the group to the selection *without* toggling expand/collapse — so it can't be used to reveal the file either.

There's no click that both preserves the existing multi-selection and reveals the collapsed contents.

**Fix:** split the hit target. Make the chevron its own dedicated control — always toggles expand/collapse, never touches selection, regardless of modifier keys. The folder name/label then behaves exactly like a file row: plain click replaces the selection with just that group, Cmd/Ctrl-click toggles it into/out of the current selection — neither touches expand state. That resolves the scenario: click the chevron to expand (selection untouched), then Cmd/Ctrl-click the newly visible file to add it.

This also makes group rows and file rows consistent (same click/Cmd-click semantics), rather than groups having a plain-click side effect files don't.

Want me to update the spec.md wording to reflect the chevron/label split?

message.content: Yes - and one addition: using the folder name to expand/collapse is nice in the single-selection case. Would it be possible to have the folder name expand/collapse if there is zero/one file currently selected and cmd/ctrl is not pressed?

content.text: Yes, that's feasible and doesn't reopen the conflict — the chevron stays as the unconditional fallback either way. The rule: on a plain (non-modifier) click on the folder name, check the selection size *before* applying the click — if it was 0 or 1, replace the selection with `{group}` and also toggle expand/collapse (the old one-click convenience); if it was already 2+, replace the selection but skip the toggle, so clicks used to build/adjust a multi-selection don't pop folders open or closed as a side effect. Cmd/Ctrl-click on the name still never toggles expand/collapse, at any selection size. Let me update spec.md with the full design.

message.content: Could the preview panel show the latest addition / removal of the selection when the user has pressed cmd/ctrl?

content.text:
Yes, and it's actually simpler than the current rule rather than more complex. Right now the preview is derived from "selection has exactly one entry and it's a previewable file" — tied to selection *size*. I'd decouple it from size entirely and instead track "the last previewable file touched by a click," independent of how many things end up selected:

- Any click on a previewable file row — plain or Cmd/Ctrl, whether it adds or removes that file from the selection — updates the preview to that file. So Cmd-clicking file B onto an existing selection shows B; Cmd-clicking file B off again (removing it) still shows B, since it was the thing you just interacted with, even though it's no longer highlighted.
- Clicks on group rows, or on non-previewable rows (corrupt/non-PDF files), don't touch the preview at all — whatever was last shown stays shown. This matches the very first pre-unification behavior (group clicks never affected preview) and avoids the panel going blank just because you're multi-selecting a batch of folders for assignment.

This drops the "selection.size === 1" condition from the preview logic entirely — one less thing coupling preview state to selection state, and it mirrors how Finder's preview column tracks the most recently focused item during a Cmd-click multi-select rather than blanking once you have more than one thing selected.

Want me to fold this into the spec.md wording?

message.content: What happens if a user selects a subfolder _and_ one of it's decendants? That would be conflicting, right?

content.text:
Not a hard conflict in the sense of "which folder wins" — since it's one batch action, the same picked folder gets applied to every selected target, so there's no disagreement about the destination at the moment you apply it. But it does create a real problem: the descendant would get its own file-level (or nested-group) override that happens to equal its parent's brand-new assignment right now, but is pinned independently — so if you later change the subfolder's assignment, that descendant won't follow along, silently diverging from what its sibling files do. It'd also show up in the UI as an explicit "own" assignment (filled badge + clear button) rather than inherited, which is misleading since the user's intent was almost certainly "assign this whole subtree," not "give this one file a separate pin."

I'd handle it by pruning the selection before applying: when building the list of targets for the "Assign Drive folder…" action, drop any selected item that's already a descendant of another selected subfolder in the selection. Only the topmost selected item in each selected subtree actually gets an assignment; the rest inherit it normally, same as if you'd only selected the ancestor. Selecting both isn't an error — it's just redundant, and pruning makes the redundancy harmless instead of a latent trap.

Want that added to the spec?
